clue.text: Drunken announcement of breaks for booze

indicators.note: the word for breaks is said aloud with a drunk's slurred 'sh', which is how it comes out as the spirit

parts.note: snaps means breaks, as a twig snaps

explanation.surface: A tipsy speaker slurs that the bar is open for drinking breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAPS slurred by a drunk comes out as 'shnaps', the sound of the German spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong spirit, and booze is any alcoholic drink, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Where Vulcan worked with German in cast?

indicators.note: in places the German word for with inside the word for cast

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast, as at a coconut shy
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A Roman god of fire teams up with a German actor in a film cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a theatre company or molten metal, but means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulcan was the Roman blacksmith god, so his workplace is a forge, a blacksmith's workshop.

clue.text: Travellers from Berkshire leading trio lost at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leading trio lost means the first three letters of Berkshire are removed

explanation.surface: Visitors from an English county lose three of their party on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading trio lost' drops BER from BERKSHIRE, leaving KSHIRE for 'at sea' to rearrange. Berkshire is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Hikers are walkers who travel on foot through the countryside.

clue.text: Like touring state in eastern mountains

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the word for like surrounds the rest

parts.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'
Penn is short for Pennsylvania, a US state

explanation.surface: Something like a touring trip through mountains in the east of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the range of peaks running down the length of Italy.

clue.text: Busy international clubs blocking European bid twice

indicators.note: blocking means getting in the way of, so international clubs sits inside the European

parts.note: a Pole is a European, from Poland
I is international and C is clubs, the card suit

indicators.note: twice says the same two letters are used again, this time inside the bid

parts.note: an offer is a bid, as at auction

explanation.surface: International golf clubs keep blocking a European's takeover offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' means IC goes into OFFER as well as into POLE. 'Busy' is old British slang for a detective, so a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy is British slang for a detective or constable, a member of the police force.

clue.text: Forces assembled for The Last Supper, say

indicators.note: assembled means put together in a new arrangement, so the six letters of Forces are rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops gather to take part in a famous religious scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's Last Supper is a wall painting done on plaster, an example of the technique; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Carnivore of the woods distressed in middle of moorland

indicators.note: in places the word for distressed inside the centre of moorland
middle of picks the central two letters of moorland

parts.note: ate can mean worried or distressed, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: A forest predator in a sorry state is found in the heart of the moors.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE as 'distressed' comes from 'eat' meaning to worry.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is a fierce meat-eating mammal of African and Asian woodland.

clue.text: Scattered crop said to be spoilt

indicators.note: to be spoilt means ruined, so the letters of crop said are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harvest is reported to have been ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring here and there or now and then, irregular and scattered.

clue.text: Trump's unacceptable manner spoken of

parts.note: out means unacceptable, as in 'that's out'

indicators.note: spoken of signals that the word for manner is said aloud and spelt as a homophone

parts.note: way means manner, as in 'in a friendly way'

explanation.surface: A comment on a politician's offensive way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' reads as the US president but is the verb: to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump something is to beat it, as a weightier factor counts for more than another.

clue.text: Small reservoir provided by king on ruling favourably

indicators.note: in an across clue, king placed on ruling means it comes straight after it

parts.note: a party that is in is the ruling one, in power
K is the chess abbreviation for king
well means favourably, as in 'spoke well of'

explanation.surface: A water supply is granted by a monarch after a favourable judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: An ink pot sunk in an old school desk holds a small store of ink, a reservoir in miniature.

clue.text: Kentish solicitor wrapping son's presents

parts.note: Kent is in south-east England, abbreviated SE

indicators.note: wrapping means going around, so the word for solicitor encloses the letter for son

parts.note: a tout is someone who solicits custom, e.g. a ticket tout
S is the standard abbreviation for son; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A lawyer from Kent wraps up a boy's birthday gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but here it is one who solicits trade. 'Presents' is a verb, not gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out an argument is to lay it out or present it, the verb sense rather than gifts.

clue.text: Was every sane soldier ultimately involved in it?

definitions.note: it stands for the war the question asks about

indicators.note: involved means entangled, so the letters of was every sane are mixed up
ultimately picks the final letter of soldier

explanation.surface: A question whether any sane soldier would have fought in a long war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges WASEVERYSANE into SEVENYEARSWA, and 'ultimately' adds the R ending soldier. The definition is just 'it', the conflict asked about.
explanation.definitionFit: The question's 'it' points to a conflict, and this 1756-63 war drew in most of Europe's great powers.

clue.text: He'll eat his own catch and not what's thrown back

definitions.text: He'll eat his own catch and not what's thrown back

parts.note: the pronoun He is taken as written; the 'll belongs to the surface

indicators.note: thrown back says the word for 'and not' is read backwards

parts.note: 'and not' is nor, as in 'neither this nor that'

explanation.surface: An angler who keeps every fish he lands rather than releasing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the bird: unlike an angler practising catch and release, it swallows what it catches.
explanation.definitionFit: This wading bird spears fish and eats them, never releasing a catch back into the water as anglers sometimes do.

clue.text: Moving show about rebel on throne returning

indicators.note: in an across clue the rebel sitting on the throne follows it

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for throne is read in reverse

parts.note: throne is slang for a toilet, and lav is short for lavatory
Jack Cade led a rebellion against Henry VI in 1450

explanation.surface: A revolutionary returns to power in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throne' is the slang sense, the lavatory; Jack Cade is an English rebel of 1450.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalcade is a procession of riders or vehicles, a show that moves along a route.

clue.text: Running into bar during finale, penniless

indicators.note: during means within, so the word for bar sits inside the shortened finale
penniless says the letter for a penny is removed; D was the old abbreviation for a penny

parts.note: an ending is a finale
a counter is a bar where drinks are served

explanation.surface: A broke drinker reaches the pub just as the evening winds up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penniless' uses D, the old abbreviation for a penny (Latin denarius), and leaves ENING; 'during' puts the bar inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Encountering someone is meeting them by chance, the same as bumping or running into them.

clue.text: Dispose of mouse finally caught in shed

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of mouse
in places the cricket letter for caught inside the word for shed

parts.note: to radiate is to shed or give off light or heat
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A mouse is finally trapped in a garden shed and must be got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut but is a verb, give off.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out or get rid of completely, which is to dispose of.

clue.text: Scholarly accounts, second cut by half

indicators.note: cut by means split open by, so accounts is interrupted by the other pieces

parts.note: ACC is an abbreviation for accounts
A is a second, as in 'A1'; also a grade
demi- is a prefix meaning half, as in demigod

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper's ledgers, the second set halved by budget cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic means relating to scholarship and learning, as in academic research.

clue.text: Wishes to forgo initial salary

indicators.note: to forgo initial means giving up the first letter of the word for wishes

parts.note: yearnings are wishes or longings

explanation.surface: Someone longs to give up their starting pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money received for work, which for a salaried employee is their pay.

clue.text: Notice corrupt fiscal aides beginning to defect

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted, so the letters of fiscal aides are reworked
beginning to picks the opening letter of the following word, defect

explanation.surface: A bribe-taking financial assistant is spotted about to switch sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A small advertisement in a newspaper is a notice, such as one offering goods for sale.

clue.text: Carrier's chance to frame question

definitions.note: Carrier's is read as carrier is, the noun

indicators.note: to frame means to enclose, so the word for chance goes round the word for question

parts.note: a bet is a chance taken, a gamble
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A delivery driver gets a chance to set up a question.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket is a container with a handle, used to carry shopping or goods.

clue.text: Prime gay rhymes

definitions.meaning: prime means the best years, the peak of life
a pair of words rhyming with gay, a greeting and a span of daylight, which joined spell the entry

explanation.surface: Cheerful verses at their best.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful definition: HEY and DAY each rhyme with 'gay', and together they spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: One's prime is the peak period of strength or success, the golden years of a career or era.

clue.text: First of Aylesbury ducks cooked in Cardigan eatery?

indicators.note: ducks means dodges out, so the first letter of Aylesbury leaves the mixture
cooked means doctored, so the letters of in Cardigan are rearranged
First of picks the opening letter of Aylesbury

explanation.surface: Aylesbury ducks, a famous breed, being cooked in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Aylesbury ducks are a breed, but 'ducks' is a verb: A ducks out of INCARDIGAN before 'cooked' rearranges the rest. Cardigan is a Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage where passengers have meals is a place to eat, an eatery on wheels; the question mark flags the stretch.

clue.text: Charlatans claiming elevated birth

definitions.note: birth is used as a modifier, as in 'birth date'; the answer is the adjective

indicators.note: elevated in a down clue means raised up, so the hidden letters are read from bottom to top
claiming means holding within, so the letters are found inside Charlatans

explanation.surface: Fraudsters pretend to be of noble birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' reads as high-born but in a down answer means the letters run upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal means relating to birth, as in natal day or prenatal care.

clue.text: Old lady's stabbing that is senseless

indicators.note: stabbing means piercing, so grandma goes into the abbreviation for that is

parts.note: ie is id est, Latin for that is
nan is a familiar word for grandmother, an old lady; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A senseless attack by a grandmother wielding a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inane is silly and empty, without sense or meaning.

clue.text: Call up troops to seize northern province

indicators.note: to seize means to grab hold of, so the call-up word takes in the letter for northern

parts.note: to muster is to assemble or call up troops

explanation.surface: An army is mobilised to capture land in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Munster is one of the four provinces of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Munster is one of Ireland's four historic provinces, in the south-west.

clue.text: Dog-tired wife produced chops

parts.note: hacked means chopped, cut roughly

explanation.surface: An exhausted wife made cuts of meat for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacked is informal slang for utterly exhausted, the same as worn out.

clue.text: Dear officer on retirement given sheltered housing

indicators.note: given here means being placed into position, the start of the containment signal
housing means holding inside, so the reversed officer goes within the word for sheltered

parts.note: cosy means snug and sheltered

indicators.note: on retirement means going back, so the officer's abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer who retires is given a place in sheltered housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheltered housing' reads as a care home for the elderly but splits into COSY and a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means expensive, high-priced, as in 'petrol is dear'.

clue.text: Where to find Orlando at play, oddly struck with passion

parts.note: Orlando is the hero of As You Like It, set in the Forest of Arden

indicators.note: oddly struck means the odd-numbered letters are crossed out, so the even ones of at play remain

explanation.surface: An actor playing Orlando is suddenly overcome with passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at play' doubles as 'in the play' in the surface; here its even letters are kept after 'oddly struck' strikes out the odd ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting ardently is acting with fervour, eagerly and passionately.
